newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom seen erratic in near-term.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom seen erratic in near-term.

text.p: Shares in newly-floated Deutsche Telekom AG are likely to plot an erratic course over the next few days before finding a more stable trend, traders and analysts said on Monday.

The major influence on Deutsche Telekom trading in the near-term will however be the positive effect of institutions seeking to buy in the open market what they could not get in the allotment of the heavily oversubscribed issue, they said.
"That's certainly happening. We are seeing institutions, even in Germany, that only got around half of what they were after," said one analyst that did not want to be named.
Demand for the 713 million shares issued in Germany's telecoms giant outpaced supply by around five times, despite a last-minute 20 percent increase in the issue size.

The size of the demand led to an allocation among domestic and international investors that dealers described as "very thin". German investors took two-thirds of the issue, with the rest going abroad.

American and Canadian institutions took 14 percent. Opinions differed widely, however, on what further impact the stock squeeze could have on the shares, which opened at 33.20 marks before moving as high as 34.10 -- substantially above their issue price of 28.50 marks.
"This could be the highest level we will get for the shares for the next few days," one trader said, adding that he thought the share could fall back to around 30 marks.
Any small impact arising from smaller investors "stagging" -- taking quick profit from -- their initial investment in the shares could already be fizzling out, he noted.
"With the 50 pfennig special discount they got, they will already be quite pleased with the five mark per share profit they have already pocketed, thank you," he added.
Other traders said the demand for the shares was such that they expected them to reach a level of 35-36 marks by the end of the week.

"But the trend will really only be seen tomorrow (Tuesday) when we have New York and Tokyo trading as well," said one trader. New York trade in the stock is due to start on Monday, with the Japanese market following a day later.
